report:
Fresh review of crates.sage_ir.modules.expand.completeness: inspected the complete claim, eight implementation associations, four ordinary test functions, and one explicit TODO test. Captured the architectural-foundations terminal-incompleteness rationale and the source-test construction/trait-selection helpers. The current change in associated mods.rs only exposes symbol_local_item as pub(crate) and adds an association for the import ambiguity audit; its classification behavior is unchanged.

The contract requires semantic-question-specific completeness before using absent symbols as definite negative evidence, while allowing represented symbols to remain usable. mods.rs publishes represented items through local_expanded_module_items independently of conservative completeness functions. bang_macro_expansion_complete returns false for unresolved or ambiguous lookup, active attributes, depth exhaustion, malformed output and nested incomplete expansions. Unsupported derive handling is question-specific: an unrelated recognized builtin cannot hide impls of a different target trait, while unsupported/unresolved relevant derives remain incomplete. macro_invocations.rs preserves expansion failure as an Error item rather than silently returning successful empty output. builtins.rs explicitly returns None for unsupported derives or input shapes. The symbol_local_item helper maps supported local symbols to the same item kinds before and after this change.

impls.rs local_impl_candidates recursively accumulates trait-specific module completeness, missing impl trait identities and unusable impl signatures. clauses.rs carries that incomplete flag into assembly alongside represented candidates rather than inferring absence from the candidate vector. prove.rs retains it when merging both trait proofs and normalization candidates. merge.rs returns No from empty candidate evidence only when the source is complete, while a genuinely unconditional Proven answer may establish Yes despite missing alternatives. Otherwise anti_unify.rs includes an unconstrained possible source and returns Maybe; missing alternatives cannot manufacture restrictive common substitutions. These eight associated files account for the publication and solver-negative path.

The ordinary merge tests explicitly compare the same empty candidate list with complete versus incomplete input, requiring No versus Maybe, and require an unconditional Proven answer to remain Yes when incomplete. The source-driven unresolved-item-macro and malformed-item-output tests obtain the represented Marker trait and then prove ground Bool:Marker, requiring Maybe rather than No or panic. Captured helpers confirm actual source parsing and expanded-item lookup, not mocked proof results. The modules_expand_completeness TODO honestly retains the missing complete end-to-end matrix: successful expansion allowing a ground exhaustive negative, and unsupported/resource-limited expansion conservatively preventing that negative, across semantic consumers. It is not counted as executable behavioral proof; completing those cases remains prerequisite to removing TODO status.

Executed cargo test -p sage-ir --lib incomplete_source (2 passed), cargo test -p sage-ir --lib no_candidates_is_no_only_for_complete_source (1 passed), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib prevents_ground_no (8 passed). These runs include all four associated ordinary test functions; additional matching tests passed but are not substituted for missing anchor associations. No source edits or new behavioral defects resulted from this review. All ordinary and deferred evidence is accounted for and no edits are requested.
